entries.en_definition: Abdomen: The part of the body containing the digestive organs, bounded by the diaphragm and the pelvis.
Abdomen Lower: The lower portion of the abdomen, below the navel.
Abdomen Lower Part Of: Refers to the specific region in the lower area of the abdomen.
Abdomen Upper Part Of: The upper portion of the abdomen, above the navel.
Achilles Tendon: The tendon connecting the calf muscles to the heel bone.
Adam's Apple (laryngeal prominence): The protrusion in the neck, formed by the thyroid cartilage of the larynx.
Adrenal gland: A small organ on top of each kidney that produces hormones like adrenaline and cortisol.
Albumin: A protein found in blood plasma, essential for maintaining the osmotic pressure needed for proper distribution of body fluids.
Alveoli (air sacs in the lungs): Tiny sacs within our lungs that allow oxygen and carbon dioxide to move between the lungs and bloodstream.
Ankle: The joint connecting the foot with the leg.
Ankle/Ankle Bone: Refers to the bones forming the ankle joint, primarily the talus bone.
Anus: The opening at the end of the digestive tract through which solid waste leaves the body.
Aorta: The largest artery in the body, originating from the left ventricle of the heart and extending down to the abdomen.
Appendix: A small tube-like structure attached to the large intestine, with no known essential function.
Arch: Refers to the curved part of the foot, also known as the arch of the foot.
Areola: The pigmented area surrounding the nipple of the breast.
Arm: The upper limb of the body, extending from the shoulder to the wrist.
Armpit: The area under the joint where the arm connects to the shoulder, also known as the axilla.

entries.to_term: kālava, kālava kini - 'ave toto mei he mafu ki he sino kotoa
entries.en_definition: Arteries: Blood vessels that carry oxygenated blood away from the heart to the rest of the body.
Artery: A vessel that carries blood away from the heart.
Artery - Of The Teeth: Refers to the arteries supplying blood to the teeth, primarily the maxillary artery.
Astragalus (of the foot): Also known as the talus bone, it forms part of the ankle joint.
Atlas (cervical vertebra): The first cervical vertebra of the spine, supporting the skull.
Atrium (left): The upper left chamber of the heart that receives oxygenated blood from the lungs.
Atrium (right): The upper right chamber of the heart that receives deoxygenated blood from the body.
Auricle (of the heart): A small muscular appendage of each atrium in the heart.
Back: The posterior part of the human body, running from the neck to the pelvis.
Backbone: The spine or vertebral column; the series of vertebrae extending from the skull to the lower back.
Backbone/Spine: Another term for the vertebral column or spine.
Beard: The hair growing on the chin and lower cheeks of a man's face.
Belly (stomach & bowel): Refers to the abdomen, particularly the front part where the stomach and intestines are located.
Belly Button (see navel): The small, round scar on the abdomen where the umbilical cord was attached.
Belly Button (protrude): Refers to a navel that sticks out.
Biceps: The large muscle at the front of the upper arm responsible for bending the arm.
Bicuspids: The two-cusped teeth located between the canines and molars, also known as premolars.
Big Toe: The largest toe on the foot.
Bile: A digestive fluid produced by the liver and stored in the gallbladder, essential for the digestion of fats.
Bile Duct: The duct that carries bile from the liver and gallbladder to the duodenum.
Bladder: The organ that stores urine before it is excreted from the body.
Blood: The red liquid that circulates in the arteries and veins, carrying oxygen and nutrients to the body and removing waste.
Blood Clot: A thickened mass in the blood formed by platelets to stop bleeding.
Blood Vessel: Any of the tubes through which blood circulates in the body, including arteries, veins, and capillaries.
Body: The physical structure of a person or an animal, including the bones, flesh, and organs.
Body (dead): Refers to a corpse or the remains of a dead person or animal.
Bone: The hard, rigid form of connective tissue constituting most of the skeleton.
Bone Marrow, Marrow: The soft, spongy tissue in the center of bones where blood cells are produced.
Bones: The rigid organs that constitute part of the vertebrate skeleton, supporting and protecting various parts of the body.
Bottom: The lower part of something; in anatomy, often refers to the buttocks.
Bottom, Backside: Another term for the buttocks or the rear part of the body.
Bowel: The intestine, especially the lower part of the digestive system, including the large intestine.
Brain: The organ in the skull that controls all bodily functions and mental processes.
Brainstem: The central trunk of the brain, continuing downward to form the spinal cord.
Breast: The front of the chest, especially the mammary glands in women.
Breast of a Woman: Refers specifically to the mammary glands in females.
Breastbone (sternum): The long flat bone in the center of the chest to which the ribs are attached.

entries.en_term: bronchi (larger air passages in the lungs
entries.en_definition: Bronchi (larger air passages in the lungs): The major air passages of the lungs that branch off from the windpipe (trachea).

entries.en_term: bronchioles (smaller air passages in the lungs)
entries.en_definition: Bronchioles (smaller air passages in the lungs): The tiny branches of air tubes within the lungs that connect to the alveoli.
Bronchus: One of the two main branches of the trachea that lead to the lungs.
Brow: The area of the face above the eyes, including the eyebrows.
Buccal Cavity (mouth cavity): The mouth, including the space between the teeth and the inner cheeks.
Buttocks: The fleshy part of the body at the back of the hips, often referred to as the rear or backside.
Caecum: A pouch connected to the junction of the small and large intestines.
Calcaneum (of the foot): The heel bone, also known as the calcaneus.
Calcaneus: The largest bone in the foot, forming the heel.
Calf: The back portion of the lower leg.
Calf (of the leg): The muscular back part of the lower leg, primarily made up of the gastrocnemius and soleus muscles.
Canine tooth: The pointed teeth located between the incisors and premolars, used for tearing food.
Capillary: The smallest blood vessels where oxygen and nutrients are exchanged with tissues.

entries.to_term: kālava 'o e kia´ mei he mafu´
entries.en_definition: Carotic artery: A major artery in the neck that supplies blood to the brain, neck, and face.
Carpal: Refers to the bones of the wrist.
Cartilage: A flexible connective tissue found in joints, ear, nose, and other areas of the body.
Cartilage permanent: Cartilage that remains throughout life, such as the cartilage in the ear and nose.
Cartilage temporary: Cartilage that is eventually replaced by bone, such as during the development of long bones.
Cecum (beginning of large intestine): The first section of the large intestine, where the small intestine joins the large intestine.
Cell: The basic structural, functional, and biological unit of all living organisms.
Cement (of the teeth): A calcified substance covering the root of a tooth, helping to anchor it to the jawbone.
Cerebellum: A part of the brain responsible for coordinating voluntary movements and balance.
Cerebral hemisphere: One of the two halves of the brain that control different functions and processes.
Cerebrum: The largest part of the brain, responsible for cognitive functions such as thought, memory, and emotion.
Cervical Vertebrae: The seven vertebrae in the neck region of the spine.
Cervix: The lower part of the uterus that opens into the vagina.
Cheek: The soft area of the face below the eyes, above the jaw, and to the side of the nose and mouth.
Chest: The front part of the body between the neck and the abdomen, housing the heart and lungs.
Chin: The lower part of the face below the mouth, formed by the lower jawbone.

entries.en_term: chordae tendineae - tendinus cords or heart strings
entries.en_definition: Chordae tendineae (tendinous cords or heart strings): Thin, strong cords that connect the heart valves to the heart muscles, preventing them from inverting.
Clavicle (collar bone): A long bone that serves as a strut between the shoulder blade and the sternum.
Clitoris: A small, sensitive, erectile part of the female genitalia.
Coccyx (tailbone): The small, triangular bone at the base of the spinal column, composed of fused vertebrae.
Colon: The longest part of the large intestine, involved in water absorption and formation of feces.
Cornea (of the eye): The transparent, dome-shaped surface that covers the front of the eye and helps focus light.
Coronary artery (left): The artery that supplies oxygen-rich blood to the left side of the heart muscle.
Coronary artery (right): The artery that supplies oxygen-rich blood to the right side of the heart muscle.

entries.en_term: corpus callosum (nerve fibres connecting brain hemispheres)
entries.en_definition: Corpus callosum (nerve fibers connecting brain hemispheres): A thick band of nerve fibers that connects the left and right hemispheres of the brain, facilitating communication between them.
Corpuscles: Cells or cell-like structures, particularly red or white blood cells.
Cranial nerves: Twelve pairs of nerves that emerge directly from the brain and control functions such as smell, vision, and facial movements.
Cranium (skull): The bony structure that encloses and protects the brain.
Crown (of the teeth): The visible part of the tooth above the gum line.
Crutch: A support used by an individual to aid in walking, typically placed under the arms.
Cuboid (of the foot): One of the tarsal bones located on the outer side of the foot.
Cuneiform (of the hand): The wedge-shaped bones in the wrist (carpal bones) and foot (tarsal bones).
Cusps (of the teeth): The pointed or rounded projections on the chewing surface of the teeth.
Cuticle: The thin layer of skin at the base of the nails.
Deltoid (shoulder muscles): The large, triangular muscles covering the shoulder joint.
Dentin(e) (of the teeth): The hard tissue beneath the enamel and cementum of a tooth, making up the bulk of the tooth structure.
Dermis (layer of skin): The thick layer of living tissue below the epidermis, containing blood vessels, nerves, and glands.
Diaphragm: The dome-shaped muscle that separates the chest cavity from the abdominal cavity, playing a key role in breathing.

entries.to_term: uoua holisi vaha'a 'o e kete mo e fatafata´

entries.en_definition: Digestive canal/system: The system of organs responsible for processing food, absorbing nutrients, and eliminating waste.
Dorsal Vertebrae: The vertebrae located in the upper and mid-back (thoracic vertebrae).
Duodenum: The first part of the small intestine, where the stomach empties its contents.
Ear: The organ responsible for hearing and balance, divided into outer, middle, and inner sections.
Ear inner: The part of the ear containing the cochlea and semicircular canals, involved in hearing and balance.
Ear middle: The air-filled space behind the eardrum that contains the ossicles, which transmit sound vibrations.
Ear outer: The external part of the ear, including the auricle (pinna) and ear canal.
Eardrum: A thin membrane that separates the outer ear from the middle ear and vibrates in response to sound.
Earlobe: The soft, fleshy lower part of the ear.
Eggs, Ova: The female reproductive cells produced in the ovaries.
Elbow: The joint connecting the upper arm to the forearm.
Elbow joint (inner side): The inner aspect of the elbow, where the forearm muscles attach to the upper arm.
Enamel (of the teeth): The hard, outer surface layer of a tooth that provides protection.
End of penis: The tip of the male genital organ.
Endocardium (inner lining of the heart): The thin layer of tissue lining the inside of the heart chambers.
Epidermis (outer layer of skin): The outermost layer of skin, providing a protective barrier.
Epiglottis (flap in the throat): A leaf-shaped flap of cartilage that covers the windpipe during swallowing to prevent food from entering the lungs.
Esophagus/Oesophagus: The muscular tube that carries food and liquids from the throat to the stomach.
Ethmoid (of the skull): A delicate bone located at the roof of the nose, separating the nasal cavity from the brain.
External cuneiform (of the foot): One of the three cuneiform bones in the foot, located on the lateral side.
Eye: The organ of sight.
Eye pupil: The black circular opening in the center of the iris, controlling the amount of light entering the eye.
Eyeball: The spherical structure of the eye, containing the lens, retina, and other components necessary for vision.
Eyebrow: The strip of hair growing on the ridge above the eye socket.
Eyelash: The short hairs growing on the edge of the eyelids, protecting the eyes from dust and debris.
Eyelid: The movable fold of skin that covers and protects the eye.
Face: The front part of the head, including the eyes, nose, mouth, and forehead.
Faeces: Solid waste material expelled from the digestive tract through the anus.
Fallopian Tubes: The pair of tubes that carry eggs from the ovaries to the uterus.
Fat: A type of tissue that stores energy and insulates the body.
Fatty tissue: A type of body tissue that stores fat, providing energy and insulation for the body.
Feet, Foot: The lower extremities used for standing, walking, and running.
Femur (thigh bone): The longest and strongest bone in the body, extending from the hip to the knee.
A developing baby inside the womb from about eight weeks after conception until birth.

entries.en_term: fibrin - fatu vave ai e toto
entries.en_definition: Fibrin: A protein involved in blood clotting.
Fibro cartilage: A type of cartilage that is tough and flexible, found in areas like the intervertebral discs.

entries.to_term: hui 'alu mei he mu'a tui ki he va'e
entries.en_definition: Fibula (calf bone): The smaller of the two bones in the lower leg, located on the lateral side.
Finger: One of the five digits on the hand.
Little finger: The smallest finger, located on the outermost side of the hand.
Short finger (cut): A finger that has been partially amputated, resulting in a shorter length.
Thumb: The short, thick first digit of the hand, opposable to the other fingers, allowing for gripping and handling objects.
Finger bones: The phalanges, the bones of the fingers.
Finger index: The second finger, located next to the thumb.
Finger middle: The third finger, located between the index and ring fingers.
Finger pinky: The smallest finger, located on the outermost side of the hand.
Finger ring: The fourth finger, located between the middle and pinky fingers.
Fingernail: The hard, protective covering at the tip of each finger.
Fingertips: The sensitive pads at the tips of the fingers.
Fist: The hand closed tightly with the fingers curled inward.
Flesh: The soft tissue of the body, consisting of muscle and fat.
Follicles (hair roots): The small cavities in the skin where hair grows.
Foot: The lower extremity below the ankle, used for standing, walking, and running.
Foot (sole of): The bottom part of the foot.
Forearm: The part of the arm between the elbow and the wrist.
Forefinger: Another term for the index finger.
Forehead: The part of the face above the eyebrows and below the hairline.
Frontal (of the skull): The bone forming the front part of the skull and the upper part of the eye sockets.
Gall bladder: A small organ that stores bile produced by the liver.
Gastrocnemius (calf muscle): The large muscle at the back of the lower leg that forms part of the calf.
Genitals: The external organs of the reproductive system.
Gingival sulcus (of the teeth): The small gap between the teeth and gums.
Gland: An organ that produces and releases substances, such as hormones or enzymes.
Glands: Organs that secrete hormones, enzymes, or other substances.
Glottis (part of the larynx): The part of the larynx containing the vocal cords, responsible for sound production.
Groin: The area of the body where the thigh meets the abdomen.
Gum: The soft tissue that surrounds and supports the teeth.
Hair: The thread-like strands growing from the skin, particularly on the head.
Hair of the head: The hair that grows on the scalp.
Hamstring: The muscles at the back of the thigh that bend the knee and extend the hip.
Hand: The part of the body at the end of the arm, used for grasping and manipulating objects.
Hand - back of the: The dorsal side of the hand, opposite the palm.
Hand - front of the hand: The palmar side of the hand, where the palm is located.
Hand bones (see metacarpal): The bones that make up the hand, including the metacarpals.
Head: The uppermost part of the body, containing the brain, eyes, ears, nose, and mouth.

entries.to_term: ongo'i, telinga tu'a, telinga veiveiua, telinga loto
entries.en_definition: Hearing: The sense that detects sound.
Heart: The muscular organ that pumps blood throughout the body.
Heel: The back part of the foot, below the ankle.
Hip: The area on either side of the pelvis, where the thigh bone meets the pelvis.
Hip bone: The large, flat bone forming the sides of the pelvis.
Hormone: A chemical messenger produced by glands that regulates various functions in the body.
Humerus (upper arm bone): The bone in the upper arm, extending from the shoulder to the elbow.
Ilium (part of the pelvis): The large, broad bone forming the upper part of the pelvis.
Incisor: A type of tooth located at the front of the mouth, used for cutting food.
Index finger: The second finger, located next to the thumb.
Inferior vena cava: The large vein that carries deoxygenated blood from the lower body to the heart.
Intestine - large: The part of the digestive system that absorbs water and forms feces.
Intestine: The digestive tube that extends from the stomach to the anus, including both the small and large intestines.
Intestine - small: The part of the digestive system where most digestion and absorption of nutrients occurs.
Internal Organs: Vital body parts located inside the body, such as the heart, lungs, liver, kidneys, and intestines, that perform essential functions for survival.
Iris: The colored part of the eye that controls the size of the pupil.
Ischium: The lower, curved part of the pelvis, on which the body sits.
Jaw: The bones forming the framework of the mouth, including the upper jaw (maxilla) and lower jaw (mandible).
Jawbone: Another term for the mandible, the lower jawbone.
Jejunum: The middle section of the small intestine.
Joints: The points where two or more bones meet, allowing for movement.

entries.to_term: kālava 'o e kia ki he mafu´
entries.en_definition: Jugular vein: The large vein in the neck that carries blood from the head to the heart.
Kidney: The organ that filters waste from the blood and produces urine.
Knee: The joint connecting the thigh to the lower leg.
Knee cap: The patella, the small bone that covers the knee joint.
Knuckle: The joint of a finger, especially where the finger bends.
Lachrymal (of the face): Relating to the glands that produce tears.
Large Instestine: The part of the digestive system that absorbs water and forms feces.
Larynx: The voice box, located in the throat, containing the vocal cords.
Left auricle: The left upper chamber of the heart that receives oxygenated blood from the lungs.
Left ventricle: The left lower chamber of the heart that pumps oxygenated blood to the body.
Leg: The lower limb of the body, from the hip to the foot.
Ligament: A band of tough, fibrous tissue that connects bones or supports organs.
Lips: The fleshy, movable parts of the mouth that form the opening.
Liver: A large organ that processes nutrients, detoxifies the blood, and produces bile.
Loins: The lower part of the back and the sides of the body between the ribs and pelvis.
Lower jaw: The mandible, the bone forming the lower part of the skull.
Lower maxillary (of the face): The lower jawbone or mandible.
Lumbar Vertebrae: The five vertebrae in the lower back.
Lungs: The pair of organs responsible for gas exchange, taking in oxygen and expelling carbon dioxide.
Lymph glands: Small glands that are part of the immune system, filtering lymph fluid and housing immune cells.
Malar (of the face): Relating to the cheekbone.
Marrow, Bone Marrow: The soft, spongy tissue inside bones where blood cells are produced.
Medulla oblongata: The lower part of the brainstem that controls vital functions like breathing and heart rate.
Membrane: A thin layer of tissue that covers a surface or lines a cavity or organ.
Metacarpal (hand bones): The five long bones in the hand that connect the wrist to the fingers.
Metatarsal (foot bones): The five long bones in the foot that connect the ankle to the toes.
Middle Cuneiform (of the foot): The middle of the three cuneiform bones in the foot.
Mind: The set of cognitive faculties that enables consciousness, perception, thinking, and memory.
Molars: The large, flat teeth at the back of the mouth used for grinding food.
Mouth: The opening in the face through which food is taken in and vocal sounds are emitted.
Mucous membrane: The lining of various body passages that produce mucus to protect and lubricate.
Muscle: A tissue composed of fibers that contract to produce movement in the body.
Muscles - extensor: Muscles that extend or straighten a limb or body part.
Muscles - involuntary: Muscles that contract without conscious control, such as those in the heart and digestive system.
Muscles - voluntary: Muscles that are under conscious control, such as those used for movement.
Nail: The hard, keratinous covering on the tips of fingers and toes.
Nape (back of the neck): The back of the neck, just below the hairline.
Nasal (of the face): Relating to the nose.
Nasal cavity: The hollow space behind the nose that filters, warms, and moistens inhaled air.
Navel: The belly button, the scar on the abdomen where the umbilical cord was attached.
Neck: The part of the body connecting the head to the torso.
Nerve: Bundles of fibers that transmit electrical signals between the brain and the rest of the body.
Nipple: The small projection in the center of the breast, through which milk can be secreted.
Nodes (lymph nodes): Small, bean-shaped glands that filter lymph fluid and house white blood cells.
Nose: The organ on the face that detects smell and allows for breathing.
Nostrils: The two openings of the nose through which air enters and exits.
Occipital (of the skull): The bone at the back and base of the skull.
Occiput (back of the head): The posterior part of the skull.
Occlusal (biting) surface (of the teeth): The surface of a tooth that comes into contact with the teeth of the opposite jaw during biting or chewing.
Oesophagus: The tube that carries food and liquids from the throat to the stomach.
Olecranon (elbow bone): The bony prominence of the elbow, where the humerus and ulna meet.
Optic nerve: The nerve that transmits visual information from the retina to the brain.
Organ: A part of the body that performs a specific function, such as the heart or liver.
Os Coccygis (tailbone): The small, triangular bone at the base of the spine, also known as the coccyx.
Os Hyoides: The hyoid bone, a U-shaped bone in the neck that supports the tongue.
Os Magnum (of the hand): Another term for the capitate bone, the largest of the carpal bones in the hand.
Os Sacrum: The large, triangular bone at the base of the spine, above the coccyx.
Ossa Innominata: The two large bones that make up the sides of your pelvis. They are also called hip bones
Ovary: The female reproductive organ that produces eggs and hormones.
Ovum (plural: ova): The female reproductive cell, also known as an egg.
Palate: The roof of the mouth, separating the oral and nasal cavities, and involved in taste perception.
Palate (of the face): The roof of the mouth, separating the oral and nasal cavities.
Palm: The inner surface of the hand between the fingers and the wrist.
Palm bones: The five metacarpal bones in the hand that connect the wrist to the fingers, providing structure and support to the palm.
Pancreas: The gland behind the stomach that produces digestive enzymes and insulin.
Parietal (of the skull): The two bones that form the sides and top of the skull.
Parotid: The largest of the salivary glands, located near the ear.
Patella (kneecap): The small, flat bone that covers and protects the knee joint.
Pelvis: The lower part of the torso, consisting of the hip bones, sacrum, and coccyx.
Penis: The male external reproductive organ.
Pericardium: The double-walled sac that encloses the heart.
Periodontal membrane (of the teeth): The connective tissue that surrounds the roots of the teeth and attaches them to the jawbone.
Periosteum (bony tissue) (of the teeth): The dense layer of connective tissue covering the surface of a bone.
Peritoneum (lining of the abdominal cavity): The membrane that lines the abdominal cavity and covers the abdominal organs.
Permanent cartilage: Cartilage that remains throughout life, as opposed to temporary cartilage, which is eventually replaced by bone.
Phalanges (finger bones): The bones that make up the fingers.
Phalanges (toe bones): The bones that make up the toes.
Pharynx (throat): The muscular tube that connects the mouth and nasal passages to the esophagus and larynx.
Pisiform (of the hand): A small, pea-shaped bone in the wrist.
Pituitary gland: The small gland at the base of the brain that regulates many of the body’s hormones.
Placenta: The organ that provides oxygen and nutrients to a developing fetus during pregnancy.
Pleura: The thin membrane that lines the chest cavity and covers the lungs.
Pores: The small openings in the skin through which sweat and oil are released.
Premolars: The teeth located between the canines and molars, used for grinding food.
Prepuce: The fold of skin covering the head of the penis or clitoris, commonly known as the foreskin in males.
Prostate: A male gland that produces fluid that nourishes and transports sperm.
Pubic bone: The front part of the pelvis, located just above the genitals.
Pubic hair: The hair that grows in the genital area.
Pubis: The front, lower part of the pelvic bone, located near the genital area.
Pulmonary artery: The artery that carries deoxygenated blood from the heart to the lungs.
Pulmonary vein: The vein that carries oxygenated blood from the lungs to the heart.
Pulp (of the teeth): The soft tissue inside a tooth, containing nerves and blood vessels.
Pupil (of the Eye): The black circular opening in the center of the eye that controls the amount of light entering the eye.
Radius (forearm bone): One of the two bones in the forearm, located on the thumb side.
Rectum: The final section of the large intestine, ending at the anus.
Respiratory: Relating to the system in the body responsible for breathing and the exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide.
Respiratory system: The system responsible for breathing and gas exchange, including the lungs, airways, and diaphragm.
Retina: The light-sensitive layer at the back of the eye that converts light into electrical signals sent to the brain.
Rib: A curved bone that forms part of the rib cage, protecting the chest organs like the heart and lungs.
Ribs: The bones that form the protective cage around the chest, protecting the heart and lungs.
Right auricle: The right upper chamber of the heart that receives deoxygenated blood from the body.
Right ventricle: The right lower chamber of the heart that pumps deoxygenated blood to the lungs.
Root (of the teeth): The part of a tooth embedded in the jawbone.
Sacrum (part of vertebral column): The triangular bone at the base of the spine, above the coccyx, forming part of the pelvis.
Saliva: The fluid produced by the salivary glands in the mouth, aiding in digestion and keeping the mouth moist.
Salivary gland: A gland in the mouth that produces saliva, aiding in digestion and keeping the mouth moist.
Scalp: The skin covering the top of the head, where hair grows.
Scaphoid (of the foot): A bone in the foot that is part of the tarsal bones.
Scapula (shoulder blade): The large, flat bone on the back of the shoulder.
Sclera (white of the eye): The tough, white outer layer of the eyeball.
Scrotum: The pouch of skin containing the testicles in males.
Semen: The fluid containing sperm, produced by the male reproductive organs.
Semi lunar (of the hand): Another term for the lunate bone, one of the carpal bones in the wrist.
Semicircular canals (of the ear): The three looped tubes in the inner ear that help maintain balance.
Septum: The wall dividing two cavities, such as the nasal septum that separates the nostrils.
Serum: The clear, yellowish fluid that remains after blood clots, used in various medical tests.
Female Sex Organs: The reproductive organs in females, including the ovaries, fallopian tubes, uterus, vagina, and vulva.
Male Sex Organs: The reproductive organs in males, including the testes, vas deferens, penis, and prostate gland.
Shank: The part of the leg between the knee and the ankle.
Shin: The front part of the lower leg, just below the knee.
Shoulder: The joint connecting the arm to the torso.
Side of the body: The left or right part of the torso, between the shoulders and hips.
Sinews: Tendons or ligaments, the tough, fibrous tissues that connect muscles to bones.
Sinus: A cavity within a bone or other tissue, especially in the skull.
Skeleton: The framework of bones that supports and protects the body.
Skin: The outer covering of the body, protecting it from the environment.
Skull: The bony structure that forms the head and encloses the brain.
Smell: The sense that detects odors.
Sole of foot: The bottom part of the foot.
Sphenoid (of the Skull): A bone at the base of the skull that helps form the eye sockets and supports the brain.
Spinal Cord: The bundle of nerves that runs down the spine, transmitting signals between the brain and the rest of the body.
Spleen: The organ that filters blood and helps fight infections.
Spongy: A soft, porous tissue with a honeycomb-like structure found in bones.
Sternum (breastbone): The long, flat bone in the center of the chest, connecting the ribs and protecting the heart and lungs.
Stomach: The organ in the digestive system where food is broken down by acid and enzymes.
Strand of hair: A single thread-like piece of hair.
Sublingual: Situated beneath the tongue.
Submaxillary: Relating to the lower jaw or the glands located beneath the lower jaw.

entries.to_term: vena kava lahi -mei he sino ki 'olunga
entries.en_definition: Superior vena cava: The large vein that carries deoxygenated blood from the upper body to the heart.
Suture: The line where two bones in the skull are joined.
Synovial Membrane: The lining of the joint capsule that secretes synovial fluid for lubrication.
Talus (ankle bone): The bone in the ankle that connects the foot to the leg.
Tarsal (foot bones): The seven bones in the ankle and heel that form the back part of the foot.
Taste: The sense that detects flavors in food and drink.
Teeth: The hard, calcified structures in the mouth used for biting and chewing food.
Temple: The flat area on the side of the head, behind the eyes.
Temporal (of the skull): The bones on the sides of the skull that house the structures of the ears.
Tendons: The tough, fibrous tissues that connect muscles to bones.
Testicles: The male reproductive organs that produce sperm and hormones.
Thigh: The part of the leg between the hip and the knee.

entries.en_term: thigh, upper part of the leg

entries.en_definition: Thorax: The part of the body between the neck and the abdomen, including the chest.
Throat: The passage that leads from the back of the mouth and nose to the esophagus and larynx.
Thumb: The short, thick finger on the side of the hand, opposable to the other four fingers.
Thyroid gland: The gland in the neck that regulates metabolism, growth, and development.
Tibia: The larger of the two bones in the lower leg, also known as the shinbone.
Tissue: A group of cells that perform a specific function in the body.
Toe: One of the digits on the foot.
Little toe: The smallest toe, located on the outermost side of the foot.
Toenail: The hard, protective covering on the tip of each toe.
Tongue: The muscular organ in the mouth used for tasting, swallowing, and speaking.
Tonsils: The two lymphoid tissues at the back of the throat that help fight infections.
Tooth: One of the hard, calcified structures in the mouth used for biting and chewing.
Touch: The sense that detects pressure, temperature, and pain through the skin.
Trachea (windpipe): The tube that carries air from the larynx to the lungs.
Trapezium (of the hand): One of the carpal bones in the wrist, located near the thumb.
Trapezius (shoulder muscle): A large muscle in the upper back and shoulders that helps move the shoulder blades and supports arm movements.
Trapezoid (of the hand): A small wrist bone that connects the hand to the forearm.

entries.en_definition: Triceps: A large muscle on the back of the upper arm responsible for straightening the arm.

entries.en_definition: Trunk: The central part of the body, excluding the head, arms, and legs. It includes the chest, abdomen, and back.
Ulna (forearm bone): One of the two long bones in the forearm, located on the side opposite the thumb.

entries.to_term: hui 'alu mei he kia'iva'e ki he mui'iva'e´

entries.en_definition: Umbilical Cord: The cord that connects a developing baby to its mother, providing nutrients and oxygen.
Unciform (of the hand): Another name for the hamate bone, a wrist bone with a hook-like shape.
Upper Arm: The part of the arm between the shoulder and the elbow.
Upper Jaw: The bone structure in the face that holds the upper teeth, also known as the maxilla.
Upper Maxillary (of the face): Refers to the upper jawbone, which holds the upper teeth and forms part of the nose and eye sockets.

entries.to_term: kau 'o e tangamini mei he kofuua´
entries.en_definition: Ureter: The tube that carries urine from the kidneys to the bladder.
Urethra: The tube that carries urine from the bladder out of the body.
Uterine Tubes: Also known as fallopian tubes, these are the tubes through which eggs travel from the ovaries to the uterus.
Uterus: The organ in a woman's body where a baby develops during pregnancy.
Uvula: The small, soft tissue that hangs down at the back of the throat.
Vagina: The muscular canal in a woman’s body that leads from the external genitals to the uterus.
Varicose Vein: Swollen, twisted veins that are often visible under the skin, usually in the legs.
Vas Deferens: The tube that carries sperm from the testicles to the urethra in males.

entries.to_term: kālava fakafoki toto ki he mafu´
entries.en_definition: Vein: A blood vessel that carries blood back to the heart.
Vein - of the Teeth: Small blood vessels that provide blood to the teeth.
Vein, Blood Vessel: Tubes in the body that carry blood back to the heart.
Veins: Blood vessels that carry blood back to the heart from different parts of the body.

entries.to_term: kālava fakafoki toto ki he mafu´

entries.en_definition: Vena Cava: The two largest veins in the body that carry blood from the body back to the heart.
Vena Cava (Inferior): The large vein that carries blood from the lower part of the body to the heart.
Vena Cava (Superior): The large vein that carries blood from the upper part of the body to the heart.
Ventricle (Left): The lower left chamber of the heart that pumps oxygen-rich blood to the body.
Ventricle (Right): The lower right chamber of the heart that pumps oxygen-poor blood to the lungs.
Vertebra (Backbone): A single bone in the spine that helps protect the spinal cord.
Vertebra (pl. Vertebrae): The individual bones that make up the backbone or spinal column.
Vertebrae: The series of bones that make up the spine or backbone.
Vocal Cords: The folds of tissue in the throat that vibrate to produce sound when speaking.
Vomer (of the Face): A thin bone in the nose that forms part of the nasal septum, dividing the nostrils.
Vulva: The external female genital organs, including the labia and clitoris.
Waist: The part of the body between the ribs and hips.
Waist (at the back): The back part of the waist, above the lower back.
Waist (in front): The front part of the waist, above the abdomen.
White Blood Cells: Cells in the blood that help fight infections and protect the body from disease.
Wisdom Tooth: The last molars to develop at the back of the mouth, usually in late teens or early twenties.
Womb: Another name for the uterus, where a baby grows during pregnancy.
Wrist: The joint connecting the hand to the forearm.
Wrist Bone (See Carpal): The small bones in the wrist that connect the hand to the forearm.
Xiphisternum: The lower part of the sternum (breastbone), also known as the xiphoid process.
Xiphoid Process (Part of the Sternum): The small, cartilaginous projection at the lower end of the sternum.
Zygomatic Bone (Cheekbone): The bone that forms the prominence of the cheek.
Zygomaticus (Facial Muscle): The muscle that helps lift the corners of the mouth when smiling.
Zygote: The cell formed when a sperm fertilizes an egg, the first stage of a developing embryo.
